text:
alex: Ran a 20m profiling session on 8xA100 with the latest batching heuristic (dynamic-slice v3). noticed noisy all-reduce tails and periodic stalls.
maria: can you drop the high-level numbers? per-step latency / percent time in comm vs compute?
alex: quick summary (aggregate over 1k steps):
- mean step: 24.3 ms
- compute-only (kernels): 15.6 ms (64%)
- all-reduce + host sync: 7.8 ms (32%)
- other (kv cache, scheduling): 0.9 ms (4%)

But distribution matters: 95th step = 48ms, and all 95th/99th are dominated by one or two ranks hitting big all-reduce spikes.

cheng: do you have per-rank allreduce times? that would point to skew / rendezvous issues.

alex: pasted a snippet from the custom timers (we emit NVTX + per-rank post-allreduce event):

ALLREDUCE_MS_PER_RANK: [0.92, 1.01, 1.05, 3.21, 0.98, 1.00, 1.02, 0.97]
STEP_END_GAP_MS (between earliest/ latest rank finishing compute): 2.1 ms

sam: that rank 3 spike lines up with a kernel-selection fallback we saw earlier? maybe quantized kernel on that shard fell back to fp16 path and took longer.

alex: I checked — no kernel fallback logs in nvtx zone. instead nvprof/nsys shows an extra 2.0 ms gap on host->device staging for rank 3 before the all-reduce. looks like PCIe driver queuing or host CPU jitter.
maria: interesting. so skew is not pure compute kernel variance but staging/comm startup jitter. can we see the kernel launch vs cudaEvent timings? also show nvtx stream IDs.

alex: here's the capture command i used: 
nsys profile --output=run_8x --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=1200s --capture-range=nvtx
I annotated around:
NVTX: [FORWARD_START], [KERNEL_SELECT], [KERNEL_LAUNCH], [KV_CACHE_LOOKUP], [ALLREDUCE_START], [ALLREDUCE_END], [STEP_END]

Sample output (per-step nvtx timeline, rank 3):
[FORWARD_START] 0.00 ms
[KERNEL_SELECT] 0.12 ms
[KERNEL_LAUNCH] 0.16 -> 12.8 ms
[KV_CACHE_LOOKUP] 12.85 -> 13.0 ms
(host staging) 13.01 -> 15.02 ms  <-- extra host delay
[ALLREDUCE_START] 15.03 -> 18.24 ms
[ALLREDUCE_END] 18.24 ms

other ranks show host staging 13.01 -> 13.9 ms and then allreduce start at 13.95 ms. so rank 3 enters allreduce ~1.1 ms late and then spends 2.1 ms in allreduce waiting for others (tail). leads to step 3x slower.

cheng: two hypotheses: (A) batching heuristic misaligns microbatch boundary with per-GPU buffer readiness (we sometimes pad differently across ranks), (B) OS-level CPU scheduling jitter on the host that delays DMA kickoff for that rank.

sam: to differentiate, we should force uniform microbatch slices across ranks and re-run for 1k steps. if the spike persists -> OS/drivers.

alex: SKETCHED quick runtime change to add a prefetch fence and NVTX around host staging so we can separate 'enqueue DMA' vs 'device ack':
```
// pseudo
nvtxRangePush("HOST_DMA_ENQUEUE");
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream);
cudaEventRecord(event_enqueue, stream);
// at kernel launch path
cudaEventRecord(event_kernel_start, stream);
nvtxRangePop();
```
This lets us measure host enqueue time vs device-visible start.

maria: also add a small histogram exporter for per-rank enqueue->allreduce_start gap. graph it per-host to catch machine-specific patterns.

alex: i ran an A/B quickly: v3 heuristic (current) vs v3-forced-aligned (slices pinned to equal microbatch sizes). results (200 steps):
- v3: 99th step 46 ms, 95th step 38 ms, allreduce spikes on 6% of steps
- v3-aligned: 99th 28 ms, 95th 26 ms, allreduce spikes on 0.5% of steps

cheng: that's a strong signal for heuristic misalignment. why are we misaligning? is it from the 'credit-based' batching that lets smaller sequences aggregate to different slice counts per device?

sam: yes, credit-batching tries to pack tokens per-device independently which saves tokens but can shift slice boundaries. we optimized throughput, but it may increase rendezvous skew.

maria: tradeoff: throughput vs tail latency. for production SLOs we should reduce skew. possible short-term mitigation: add an alignment pass across ranks that enforces equal microbatch counts when step latency > threshold.

alex: propose rollout plan:
1) add NVTX + events to isolate host enqueue vs device start (PR #3214) — @cheng will own.
2) instrument runtime to compute per-step microbatch-count variance across ranks and export metric 'microbatch_skew' to observability — @sam own.
3) experiment with two batching modes: "throughput" (current) and "aligned" (force same slices) and expose in config + smoke test on dedicated pool — @maria + @alex.
4) if skew persists after alignment -> escalate to infra for host-level jitter investigation.

cheng: started PR draft, adding gpu_event timers and nvtx zones. will push by EOD.

sam: i'll add the skew metric and a grafana panel. also add alert if 95th step rises > 1.5x baseline.

maria: when we flip to aligned mode for a run, let's run nsight on two different hosts to rule out machine-specific variance. @ci-bot can you schedule ephemeral dedicated run? :robot_face:

ci-bot: scheduled job r-1951123456-align-test on dedicated-8xA100-03, estimated 45m. link: https://ci.internal/jobs/1951123456

alex: thanks. last note: kernel-selection interplay — we've seen cases where quantized kernel has slightly different per-shard runtimes and if the batching packs more quantized shards on some ranks that could amplify skew. also log kernel variant per-rank per-step.

cheng: good call. adding kernel_variant nvtx tag in PR.

maria: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the run. summary for ticket: https://rwd/issue/PLT-5823 (adds timers, skew metric, aligned batching mode). (reacts :eyes:)

sam: SGTM.
